bibl.ref: Electoral roll, 1919, Division of Melbourne, Subdivision of Cardigan, 2549: Abraham Bernard, 85 Madeline Street, storekeeper

revisionDesc.change: Contributed through the contribution form by Andy May.

div.head: In the directories
div.p: Abraham or A. Bernard is listed at No. 85 Madeline Street from 1905 to 1925. He is a grocer from 1910 to 1920, and a confectioner and fruiterer in 1925. In 1915 he also has a wood yard next door at No. 87.

div.head: On the electoral rolls
div.p: Abraham Bernard, storekeeper, is on the 1905 and 1919 electoral rolls at 85 Madeline Street, with Zeprah Bernard, home duties.

div.head: Neighbours
div.p: M. M. Friedman, draper, is at No. 83 in 1905 and 1910, and Frank West's general store at No. 87 in 1905. Miss Hilda Mackay, costumier, is at No. 87 in 1920 and 1925, and L. T. Larsen, grocer, at No. 81 in 1925.

div.head: Biography
div.p: Abraham’s wife Zephra had a flirt with fame when she attempted to cast her vote at the State election in 1907, even though women did not have the right to vote until 1911. The anomaly was that her name had been printed on the electoral role in the mistaken belief that she was male.

Abraham was born c. 1851, Zephra around 1868. When she died in 1942 at the age of 74, Zephra's place of birth was given as “Bessarabia, Russia”, the majority of which now lies within present-day Moldova (2949/1942).

On vital records, Zephra’s surname is given variously as Nachmanovitz, Nachamovitch, Macchmanowit, and Lochminovitz, and sometimes she is also called Cecilia. It is unclear when the couple came to Australia, and there doesn’t seem to be a marriage record in Victoria.

When eldest daughter Clara married Samuel Rischin in 1910, she noted that she was born in 1889, gave her place of birth as “At sea off Colombo”, and her father’s occupation as accountant. Clara died in 1967.
Eva Bernard was born Carlton in 1896 (9807/1896), and married John Simon Rothfield in 1917 (6705/1917).
David Bernard was born in Carlton in 1903 (23884/1903) and died at Kew in 1935 (7578/1935).
Rachael born around 1898 (in NZ?), married Harry Rischin in 1920 (3353/1920), and died aged 61 in 1959 (15619/1959).

On a number of occasions, the Bernards ran afoul of the Pure Food Act 1905 which controlled “adulteration or false description” of foodstuffs, including milk. In 1914, Abraham (grocer of Madeline Street) was convicted at the Carlton Court of selling milk that contained 20% water, and fined £5 and costs, despite Zephra saying that “she only sold about three quarts of milk daily, and she never interfered with it”. The Court determined that “the case was a gross one, and the poor people living in the locality must be protected” (The Age, 29 October 1914: 8).
The following year, Abraham was described as a “retail dairyman” when he was again convicted of selling milk containing 10% added water. [The Herald, 23 August 1916: 3].
In 1917, Abraham (general grocer of Madeline Street) and his daughter Eva were fined for “feloniously” receiving stolen goods — a box containing Hudson’s extract of soap and other articles
